transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Marta Alvarez (CTO, Harbor), Kyle Chen (Head Infra), Priyanka Rao (Procurement), Evan Mills (ML Eng)

Summary: quick renewal check-in to discuss capacity upgrade, adding EU region, pricing for 12 vs 24 month extension, and next steps for security docs + benchmark. Customer asked clarifying questions about data residency, VPC/on-prem, KMS and fallback policies. Agreed to run a benchmark and share updated quote and contract addendum.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off. Hi Marta, Kyle, Priyanka, Evan. This is just our renewal and expansion check-in, want to cover capacity lift, EU region add, and term options.
[00:12] Marta (Harbor): thanks Jordan. yeah, we wanted to see numbers and timelines — we've been pretty happy with the performance but Q1 pushed us over the committed throughput.
[00:20] Kyle (Harbor): hi, quick note — QPS peaked at 3.2k last week during our promo. We need to avoid throttling; curious about Dedicated bump and autoscale.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): hey Kyle, Priya here from the SE team — we looked at your telemetry, that spike aligns with cache miss patterns, we can tune KV cache and batching to mitigate but for headroom a Dedicated capacity bump is sensible.
[00:45] Evan (Harbor): do you have an estimate of cost impact if we increase to the next reserved tier?
[00:52] Jordan: good question. I'll share the quote but ballpark — moving one GPU pool up adds about 18-25% to monthly commit depending on model mix; with a 24-month term we can pass more discount.
[01:05] Marta: Marta — what about adding EU region? We need processing in Ireland for data residency and latency to EU storefronts.
[01:12] Samir (CSM): adding EU region is supported — we can mirror Dedicated capacity in eu-west and route by geo. There is a lead time for provisioning, typically 10-14 business days for dedicated pools, faster for hosted but hosted doesn't give the same isolation.
[01:30] Kyle: procurement will want clarity on SLA and failover if eu-west goes down; can we do cross-region fallback to US with encryption in transit and at rest?
[01:40] Priya: yes, we have smart routing — can failover to a US region under policy, you can restrict model variants for the failover path. Data in flight is encrypted; for at-rest you can use KMS in region or customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
[01:55] Kyle: are there limitations when using customer KMS across regions?
[02:00] Priya: minor. If you provision a customer-managed key in EU you'll need KMS endpoints available; for cross-region failover you can either replicate keys or use per-region keys and accept that data written in failover will be subject to that key. We'll share the security doc and KMS pattern recommendations.
[02:18] Marta: can you also confirm SOC 2 scope and audit dates — procurement needs the attestation before we sign a longer term.
[02:25] Jordan: yes — we'll share our latest SOC 2 report and pen test summary. I'll attach the security pack after this meeting.
[02:33] Priyanka Rao (Harbor procurement): on pricing, we need a fixed commit vs consumption mix — Harbor prefers predictability. If we go 24 months can you give a steady monthly commit with overage terms?
[02:44] Jordan: absolutely. We can propose a committed GPU-hour pool with defined overage rates, and an annual true-up. For 24-months we can do a stepped discount: 10% for 12-months, 15% for 24, and an additional rebate if you extend to multiple regions.
[03:00] Evan: can we get an example math for our typical model mix (embedding + chat)? Our traffic is 60% chat gen, 30% embeddings, 10% re-rank.
[03:07] Priya: we'll include a modeled cost per million tokens in the quote. Also caching recommendations can drop embeddings costs significantly if you use prefix cache on repeated lookups.
[03:18] Kyle: around PII — some chat requests include customer emails and order ids; are logs retained by Redwood for hosted? We want minimal retention or a purge policy.
[03:28] Samir: retention is configurable; for Private you control logs. For Hosted we can set shorter retention or opt-out for specific endpoints; audit logs can be exported to your S3. We'll share the exact retention controls.
[03:40] Marta: ok good. Security seems fine as long as docs match. On timelines, if we sign addendum this month when can extra capacity be live?
[03:48] Priya: for Dedicated EU pool provisioning plus capacity sizing, approximately two weeks after signed PO. If we do hosted burst it can be same-day but not isolated.
[03:58] Jordan: if you want the Dedicated -- we recommend starting with a modest reserved bump + autoscale burst for spikes, then evaluate after the benchmark. That minimizes initial commit.
[04:10] Evan: benchmark — can Redwood run the benchmark with our test set to measure p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens? We'd like to baseline before committing.
[04:18] Priya: yes. Priya will run an A/B: current Dedicated config vs proposed bumped pool and EU region. We'll measure p50/p95, token cost and tail latency. Need your test set and expected concurrency pattern.
[04:30] Marta: I'll share a sanitized test set (no PII) by tomorrow.
[04:34] Priyanka Rao: procurement will need contract addendum for the 24-month option and details for auto-renew and termination penalties.
[04:43] Jordan: noted. Samir will draft a renewal addendum — we can include the discount tiers and the auto-scaling policy.
[04:50] Kyle: on model variants — we use a mix of open models and a custom fine-tuned reranker. For the reranker we want to ensure model pins and KV cache behavior is deterministic when we scale horizontally. Any caveats?
[05:03] Priya: horizontal scaling is compatible with pinned model versions; KV cache is per-host but we have prefix caching to reduce misses. For consistent rerank behavior we recommend session affinity or using a shared KV replication strategy; we'll include configuration notes.
[05:18] Marta: any risks with quantization or accuracy drift if you suggest quantized model nodes for cost savings?
[05:25] Priya: small risk — quantization profiles are model-specific. Our Optimize recommendations include quality regressions and rollback plan. We run evals on your prompt set to quantify QA impact before enabling quantized pools.
[05:38] Evan: perfect. For the benchmark can you also include a run with quantized variant so we can see cost vs quality?
[05:44] Priya: yes, we'll include an A/B with the quantized profile for the main gen model.
[05:49] Jordan: recap and timeline: Jordan sends updated quote + security docs by Wed 2026-03-25; Priya schedules benchmark week of 2026-03-29; Samir drafts contract addendum by 2026-03-30; Marta to confirm peak QPS and share sanitized test set by 2026-03-23. Follow-up exec call week of 2026-04-05 to finalize.
[06:10] Marta: that works. Anything else on the commercial side?
[06:14] Priyanka Rao: just one more — we'd like a clause for performance credits if p95 latency exceeds SLO more than X days per quarter. Can you propose language?
[06:24] Samir: yes we'll propose a simple SLO/credit structure in the addendum.
[06:29] Jordan: great. thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:33] Marta: thanks, appreciate it.

End of transcript.
